Map each node in the provided diagram to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change diagram text or layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (input-path):
Map n24-n37 (key/mouse/paste/io writing) with line numbered file ranges. Return JSON partial.

    12	/// Options that affect mouse encoding behavior and provide runtime context.
    13	pub const Options = struct {
    14	    /// Terminal mouse reporting mode (X10, normal, button, any).
    15	    event: terminal.MouseEvent = .none,
    16	
    17	    /// Terminal mouse reporting format.
    18	    format: terminal.MouseFormat = .x10,
    19	
    20	    /// Full renderer size used to convert surface-space pixel positions
    21	    /// into grid cell coordinates (for most formats) and terminal-space
    22	    /// pixel coordinates (for SGR-Pixels), as well as to determine
    23	    /// whether a position falls outside the visible viewport.
    24	    size: renderer_size.Size,
    25	
    26	    /// Whether any mouse button is currently pressed. When a motion
    27	    /// event occurs outside the viewport, it is only reported if a
    28	    /// button is held down and the event mode supports motion tracking.
    29	    /// Without this, out-of-viewport motions are silently dropped.
    30	    ///
    31	    /// This should reflect the state of the current event as well, so
    32	    /// if the encoded event is a button press, this should be true.
    33	    any_button_pressed: bool = false,
    34	
    35	    /// Last reported viewport cell for motion deduplication.
    36	    /// If null, motion deduplication state is not tracked.
    37	    last_cell: ?*?point.Coordinate = null,
    38	
    39	    /// Initialize from terminal and renderer state. The caller may still
    40	    /// set any_button_pressed and last_cell on the returned value.
    41	    pub fn fromTerminal(
    42	        t: *const Terminal,
    43	        size: renderer_size.Size,
    44	    ) Options {
    45	        return .{
    46	            .event = t.flags.mouse_event,
    47	            .format = t.flags.mouse_format,
    48	            .size = size,
    49	        };
    50	    }
    51	};
    52	
    53	/// A normalized mouse event for protocol encoding.
    54	pub const Event = struct {
    55	    /// The action of this mouse event.
    56	    action: mouse.Action = .press,
    57	
    58	    /// The button involved in this event. This can be null in the
    59	    /// case of a motion action with no pressed buttons.
    60	    button: ?mouse.Button = null,
    61	
    62	    /// Keyboard modifiers held during this event.

   414	    if (exec.exited) return;

   417	    // our cached buffers that we can queue to the stream.
